triples.relationship: Moral juxtaposition: peaceful speech alongside evil conduct
triples.rationale: Micah places hands prepared for evil beside the ruler's request and the judge's peaceful words. The psalm explicitly describes people who speak peace to neighbors while harboring evils and asks that they receive according to their works and hands. Both set peaceful speech beside evil conduct or intentions. The psalm's explicit inner duplicity is not used to insert a bribe or resolve every pronoun and unfinished clause in Micah.
triples.source_text: They prepare their hands for evil; the ruler asks, and the judge spoke peaceful words—it is his soul’s desire. And I will remove

target_units.text: Do not drag my soul away together with sinners, and do not destroy me together with those working injustice, who speak peace with their neighbors while evils are in their hearts.
Give them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their practices; give them according to the works of their hands; repay their recompense to them.

triples.rationale: Micah names a day of brick plastering and immediately calls that day obliteration, followed by cities being leveled. Ezekiel describes a wall built and coated under a false assurance of peace, then falling when God tears it down. Both place surface construction or coating beside announced destruction. Micah's brick plastering is not rewritten as restored walls, and Ezekiel's particular wall, coating and storm are not identified as Micah's event or as the ordinances being rubbed away.
triples.source_text: on a day of brick plastering. That day is your obliteration, and it will rub away your ordinances—

target_units.text: Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.
And behold, the wall has fallen! Will they not say to you, ‘Where is your coating with which you coated it?’
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will unleash an upending blast with wrath; a flooding downpour will come in My anger, and I will bring the projectile stones in wrath for complete destruction,

and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
